title: Infleqtion and Partners Build Optical Cavity Prototype to Shrink Quantum Sensors
key_facts: Infleqtion (NYSE: INFQ), with Honeywell Aerospace and UC Santa Barbara professor Daniel Blumenthal, developed a chip-scale optical cavity prototype
Made on a silicon nitride chip at Honeywell Aerospace's photonics foundry
An optical cavity helps keep lasers stable in quantum computers, clocks and sensors; until now they were large tabletop instruments
Companies say it can be made at scale in existing commercial foundries
Near-term uses named: precision navigation and atomic timing for data centers and cell towers
Infleqtion CTO Pranav Gokhale called it an important step toward smaller, manufacturable systems
No performance figures given; text is a press release
quote_evidence: An optical cavity is a piece of hardware that helps the lasers in quantum computers, clocks, and sensors perform better.
The prototype reduces the space needed to keep lasers stable inside quantum systems.
why_it_matters_hint: A prototype that could help quantum sensors and clocks shrink from lab benches toward handheld size.
